name: Riverside County Treasurer-Tax Collector
notes: Researched 2026-10-10 from public countytreasurer.org pages (Internet Archive snapshots; the live site is behind a Cloudflare challenge) and the public PublicAccessNow e-billing terms page; no sign-in, no lookup, no form. Online payments (eCheck free, cards with a convenience fee whose amount is not published on the pages read, so no card fee is charged in the mock and it is listed in fees.notes) via ca-riverside-ttc.publicaccessnow.com; phone (951) 955-3900 or (877) 748-2689, card only; mail (check payable to the Tax Collector, PIN on the check) P.O. Box 12005, Riverside, CA 92502-2205. Two installments: due Nov 1 / Feb 1, delinquent after 5 p.m. Dec 10 / Apr 10; 10% penalty, plus $38.06 administrative charge on the second. The county cannot take more than two payments a year; monthly payments only through the endorsed third-party Easy Smart Pay (1.99%), so AutoPay is unsupported. E-billing requires a registered portal account; cancel online or by email. Installment plan of redemption only for tax-defaulted property (20% down, five years, mailed application). Email sign-in in the mock is synthetic. Reviewed 2026-10-10: How To Pay Your Taxes and Current Secured pages re-read live in a headless browser.

guest_pay.note: Search for the bill and pay online by eCheck (no fee) or Visa, MasterCard, Discover or American Express (convenience fee added).

autopay.note: The county can only accept the two installments each year. For monthly payments, use an impound account with your lender or the county-endorsed third-party Easy Smart Pay (1.99% fee).

paperless.note: Register on the payment site and accept the e-billing terms to get future annual bills by email instead of paper. Cancel by logging in or by emailing the office.

pay_by_phone.note: Credit or debit card only; call (951) 955-3900 (desert area (877) 748-2689) and choose the card payment option.

pay_by_mail.note: Mail a check or money order payable to the Tax Collector, with your PIN written on it, to P.O. Box 12005, Riverside, CA 92502-2205.

payment_arrangement.note: Current-year taxes cannot go on a plan. For tax-defaulted property, an installment plan of redemption needs at least 20% down and a signed, mailed application.

notes: Credit and debit card payments carry a convenience fee set by the processor; the amount is not published on the Tax Collector's pages.

help.title: How to pay your taxes
paragraphs: Pay online by e-check at no cost, or by Visa, MasterCard, Discover or American Express with a convenience fee added to each card payment. You can also pay straight from your bank account by signing in with your online banking.

By phone, call (951) 955-3900, or (877) 748-2689 from the desert area, and choose the card payment option; phone payments are card only. By mail, send a check or money order payable to the Tax Collector with your PIN written on it to P.O. Box 12005, Riverside, CA 92502-2205, using the envelopes that came with the bill. Card payments are not accepted by mail.

If you pay through home banking, make the payment to Riverside County Treasurer-Tax Collector with the bill number or PIN in the account field, and send it 5 to 7 days early: it must arrive by the delinquent date. Postdated checks are not held.

help.title: Due dates and penalties
paragraphs: Annual bills are mailed by November 1 and can be paid in two installments. The first is due November 1 and becomes delinquent at 5 p.m. on December 10; the second is due February 1 and becomes delinquent at 5 p.m. on April 10. You may pay the whole bill with the first installment.

A late first installment gets a 10% penalty. A late second installment gets a 10% penalty plus a $38.06 administrative charge, and the second cannot be paid before the first. Taxes still unpaid at 5 p.m. on June 30 default and add further penalties of 1.5% a month. If a delinquent date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.

help.title: Monthly payments and Easy Smart Pay
paragraphs: The Tax Collector's systems accept only the two installments each year. To spread the cost monthly, you can add the taxes to a lender impound account, save monthly in your own account, or use Easy Smart Pay.

Easy Smart Pay is a separate company the county endorses but is not affiliated with. It collects monthly ACH or card payments (currently a 1.99% fee) and forwards them to the county at the due dates. It does not cover supplemental taxes, and the November 1/December 10 and February 1/April 10 dates still apply.

help.title: E-billing
paragraphs: Registered users of the payment site can sign up to receive future annual tax bills by email instead of paper. You must accept the e-billing terms and confirm the email sent to you within 24 hours.
You do not need e-billing to pay online. Parcels are removed from e-billing automatically when ownership changes. Cancel at any time by logging in or by emailing the Treasurer-Tax Collector.

help.title: Installment plan for defaulted taxes
paragraphs: If your property is tax-defaulted (unpaid after June 30), you can open a five-year installment plan of redemption by paying at least 20% of the redemption amount, paying the current year's taxes, and signing and submitting the Installment Payment Plan Application and Agreement.

Each year by April 10 you must pay at least 20% plus interest of 1.5% a month on the unpaid balance and an annual maintenance fee, along with that year's taxes. Missing a payment defaults the plan. There is a start-up fee each time a plan is opened.

extra.intent: Using the Riverside County Treasurer-Tax Collector website's help pages, find the administrative charge added (besides the 10% penalty) when the second property tax installment is late. Do not make a payment or change any settings.
